A.note: Google selects and shares with external experts at its discretion (A.3); nothing statutory or contractually enforceable is documented.

R.note: Only the lab's naming of the firm reaches the public; engagement terms bar or do not provide for independent publication.

resolution.note: Floor 3 (dreadnode.09, M.1: open benchmark code) against cap 1 (dreadnode.08: the frontier-lab engagement is closed). The organization's methods are public in prose and in an open self-directed benchmark, so it is not 'summaries only'; but the evaluation work this ledger scores, the Gemini engagement, publishes no methods, so open code for a separate benchmark does not reach anchor 3 for the organization. Anchor 2, methods described in prose, is the organization-level reading, and matches how Gray Swan (papers plus partly public Arena) and Scale (partly public leaderboards, closed government work) are scored. Gap: RULES has no rule for combining engagement-level closure with open self-directed benchmarks.

dissent.lower: Publication rights (1 to 0). Nothing from the Gemini engagement has reached the public: no summary, no finding, only the firm's name in Google's launch post and a spokesperson's sentence to Time. A name mention is not a lab-edited summary. Anchor 0 reads 'no publication, or lab approval required', and on the documented record there is no publication at all.
dissent.higher: Access depth (1 to 2). Google's external-testing programme shares pre-release models with selected experts for structured testing over a period before launch, and Dreadnode was named for both Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3. If the engagement ran for weeks against a pre-release checkpoint, that is extended-time access, anchor 2, rather than a one-off pre-release API test.

resolution.note: See assessments.M.resolution: engagement-level closure (cap 1) against open self-directed benchmark code (floor 3); resolved at anchor 2, methods described in prose, consistent with Gray Swan and Scale.
